back2basics.text: An electoral roll is an official list of eligible voters in a constituency. Voter registration involves verifying eligibility and including names in the roll to enable participation in elections. The Election Commission of India oversees the preparation and revision of electoral rolls to ensure accuracy and inclusiveness, using forms like Form 6 for new registrations and Form 8 for shifting addresses within constituencies.

body.label: Active inclusion efforts
body.text: The ECI assured the Supreme Court that it remains alert to the need to include all eligible voters, especially those wrongly left out as absent, shifted, dead, or duplicate in draft electoral rolls.

body.label: Submission of forms simplified
body.text: Voters who have shifted within the same state need not submit Form 8; instead, they can submit an Enumeration Form (Annexure A) with a statement of their new address and proof to the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) or Assistant ERO.

body.label: Online and offline options
body.text: Voters can submit forms in person, through family members, or online with e-sign on the ECINET portal, including a facility to book a call with Booth Level Officers (BLOs).

body.label: Processing and re-inclusion
body.text: Enumeration Forms submitted by left-out electors are processed according to the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, with the same Elector Photo Identity Card (EPIC) number reassigned to them.

sections.heading: What measures has the ECI taken to ensure voters find their names on electoral rolls?

body.label: Directions to States and UTs
body.text: The ECI issued directions on November 6, 2026, to Chief Electoral Officers to allow submission of Enumeration Forms during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

body.label: Display of left-out voters
body.text: Booth-wise lists of left-out electors marked as absent, shifted, dead, or duplicate are displayed with probable reasons for non-inclusion to enhance transparency.

body.label: Oversight of IT Division
body.text: A senior Deputy Election Commissioner (DEC) was assigned oversight of the ECI’s IT Division following a new work order on November 4, 2026, addressing concerns about bypassing DEC-level supervision.

body.label: Avoiding duplication
body.text: A mechanism is in place to ensure no eligible elector is deprived of inclusion while avoiding duplication in enrolment.

sections.heading: How is the ECI addressing concerns about electoral roll accuracy and oversight?

body.label: Petitioners’ concerns
body.text: Activists raised concerns that previously registered voters excluded in draft rolls were being forced to submit Form 6, meant for new voters, risking criminal prosecution under the Representation of the People Act, 1950.

body.label: ECI’s clarification
body.text: The ECI clarified that voters who had already submitted Form 6 need not submit the Enumeration Form again and their applications would be processed without fear of prosecution.

sections.heading: What controversy did the ECI clarify regarding voter re-inclusion procedures?

body.label: Overall export growth
body.text: India’s total exports increased 16.66% to US$ 568.84 billion during April-October FY 2026-27 compared to the previous year, with merchandise exports growing 21.96% and services exports 10.93%.

body.label: Monthly performance
body.text: Exports recorded positive year-on-year growth every month, including a 29.90% rise in October 2026, with merchandise exports surging 45.06% and services exports growing about 15.2%.

body.label: Sectoral growth
body.text: Seven of the top ten export categories showed double-digit growth, including other cereals (109.74%), petroleum products (47.71%), electronic goods (46.92%), and engineering goods (22%).

body.label: Services sector strength
body.text: Services exports grew at a compound annual rate of 10.3% between 2015 and 2025, outpacing the global average, and accounted for about 45.7% of total exports in April-October FY 2026-27.

sections.heading: What are the key features of India’s export growth in FY 2026-27?

body.label: Growth across markets
body.text: Eight of the ten largest merchandise export destinations recorded double-digit growth, with Singapore (107.50%), Malaysia (106.87%), Spain (88.38%), and South Africa (62.20%) among the top performers.

body.label: New product-market pairs
body.text: India added 1,985 new product-country export pairs during April-September FY 2026-27, generating US$ 622.1 million in exports across 116 product groups and 229 countries.

body.label: Regional specialties
body.text: Local products like organic palmyra jaggery powder, Sinduri pomegranates, and GI-tagged Tandur red gram reached new international markets such as Bulgaria, Dubai, and Australia.

body.label: Trade agreement partners

body.label: Employment and labour market
body.text: Labour force participation and employment rates improved in both rural and urban areas during 2026, with unemployment declining to 5.1% in July-September.

body.label: Poverty reduction
body.text: Economic growth, supported by exports, contributed to reducing poverty from 57.7% in 2011 to 16.1% in 2023 for those living under US$ 4.20 a day.

body.label: Foreign investment and reserves
body.text: Net foreign direct investment inflows rose to US$ 8.8 billion in April-September 2026, and foreign exchange reserves stood at US$ 719.55 billion, strengthening India’s external position.

sections.heading: Why does India’s export growth matter for economic development?

body.label: Legal framework
body.text: The Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Act, 1992 and the Foreign Trade Policy 2023 provide the legal and policy foundation for export promotion.

body.label: Export facilitation schemes
body.text: Schemes like Advance Authorisation, Duty Free Import Authorisation, and Export Promotion Capital Goods allow duty-free imports of inputs and capital goods for exports.

body.label: Tax remission schemes
body.text: RoDTEP and RoSCTL refund unrebated taxes and levies on exports, benefiting thousands of exporters, especially MSMEs.

body.label: Districts as Export Hubs
body.text: The DEH initiative promotes district-level export planning to enhance competitiveness and market access for local enterprises.

body.label: Export Promotion Mission
body.text: Launched in November 2025 with an outlay of ₹25,060 crore, EPM integrates financial and non-financial support to strengthen export competitiveness and generate employment.
